narrative.overview: This is the visual language of a creative agency's draft room, not an enterprise dashboard: work is shown honestly at whatever stage it's actually in — a blank shot-grid, a row of skeleton bars standing in for copy that doesn't exist yet — rather than dressed up with a spinner or a stock icon pretending to be more finished than it is. The product's whole positioning (one brief in, one coherent campaign out, nothing final without human approval) shows up visually as restraint: one calm neutral canvas, one confident accent spent on the things that actually need it, and a small, deliberate family of secondary/accent colors used to give each area its own identity without the page turning into a rainbow. The system is restrained, confident, and quietly colorful. It explicitly rejects the generic enterprise SaaS dashboard and the generic AI-generated UI cliche (purple/pink gradient blobs, spinning loaders, icon-tile grids). Depth is structural, not atmospheric.
keyCharacteristics: Draft-honest content: placeholders look like drafts of their real shape, never a generic spinner or icon.
One confident accent per moment: color is spent deliberately, not spread evenly.
Structural depth: shadow tiers sell real layering, not ambient decoration.
Quiet chrome, loud state: resting UI stays close to invisible; state changes are where contrast lives.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Any single moment on screen earns exactly one confident color decision. Never stack two accent colors as competing focal points in the same component.

rules.name: The Status-Is-Not-Decoration Rule
rules.body: Signal Amber is reserved for status communication and never reused as a decorative icon-badge color.

rules.name: The Large-Input Rule
rules.body: Input text renders at body size, never smaller than its own label implies.

rules.name: The Front-of-Form Rule
rules.body: The watch column's shadow tier is always at least one step heavier than anything in the write column.

dos: Do show unfinished content as an honest draft of its own shape — never a spinner, a generic icon, or a progress bar.
Do spend shadow deliberately — a heavier tier means structurally in front, not just decorative.
Do keep resting UI quiet so state changes are where contrast lives.
Do give each functional area its own accent identity from the established five-color family.
donts: Don't use a spinning loader or fake progress indicator to represent AI thinking — the one exception is a real in-flight network request on the primary CTA.
Don't introduce a sixth accent color or new gradient combination without updating DESIGN.md.
Don't wrap every section in its own bordered/shadowed box by default.
Don't use Whisper Lavender as a surface fill or gradient stop.
